title.zh: 卷167 表七 外戚表
title.raw: 卷167 表七 外戚表

sentences.zh: 序 班書始立外戚恩澤侯表，《遼》、《明》二史因之。

translations.literal: Preface: Ban Gu's History first established the table of Marquises Enfeoffed through Favor to Imperial In-Laws; the Histories of Liao and Ming followed this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the preface to his History, Ban Gu was the first to establish a table of noble ranks granted to imperial in-laws as a mark of imperial favor; the Liao and Ming histories adopted the same model.

sentences.zh: 遼外戚不皆有封爵，然世選北府宰相預政事，明則揚、徐二王僅假虛號，自後皆封侯、伯。

translations.literal: Liao imperial in-laws did not all receive enfeoffments, yet generation after generation they were chosen as chancellors of the Northern Administration and took part in government; under the Ming, only the kings of Yang and Xu bore empty titles, and thereafter all were enfeoffed as marquises or earls.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liao, not every imperial in-law held a noble rank, yet the clan was generation after generation chosen for the chancellorship of the Northern Administration and took part in state affairs. Under the Ming, only the Yang and Xu kings held nominal titles; after them, in-laws were enfeoffed as marquises or earls.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，詔不得與汗馬餘勳並列，惟分封大邑，帶礪相承，未嘗區以別也。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing reign, an edict barred them from being ranked alongside those who had earned merit through warhorses and sweat; they were granted only large fiefs passed down with iron covenant and grinding stone, and were never set apart in a distinct category.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, an edict barred them from being ranked alongside those who had earned merit in war; they received only large fiefs passed down in perpetuity, and were never placed in a separate category.

sentences.zh: 清初，太祖娶於葉赫，草昧干戈，制度未備。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, the Taizu married into Yehe; amid the founding chaos of warfare, institutions were not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing, the Taizu married into Yehe; amid the turmoil of founding the dynasty by force of arms, institutions were not yet in place.

sentences.zh: 太宗、世祖娶於蒙古，追進崇封，外戚恩澤自此始。

translations.literal: The Taizong and Shizu married from Mongolia; posthumous advancement to exalted enfeoffments followed, and favor to imperial in-laws began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong and Shizu took wives from Mongolia; posthumous advancement to exalted noble ranks followed, and imperial favor to in-laws began from this time.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，世宗詔定外戚爲承恩公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, the Shizong decreed that imperial in-laws should be titled Duke Who Receives Imperial Grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, the Shizong decreed that imperial in-laws should hold the title Duke Who Receives Imperial Grace.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年，高宗又詔后族承恩與佐命功臣櫛風沐雨、拓土開疆者，實難並論，俱改爲三等公。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong, the Gaozong again decreed that the empress's kin granted Cheng'en could scarcely be mentioned in the same breath as founding ministers who had braved wind and rain to open territory; all were changed to third-rank duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Qianlong, the Gaozong again decreed that empresses' kin who received imperial grace could not be ranked alongside founding ministers who had braved hardship to open new lands; all such titles were reduced to third-rank duke.

sentences.zh: 名既專屬，等復殊裁，抑制防視，明尤肅用，是終清世外家皆謹守法度，無預政事者，不可謂非詒謀之善也。

translations.literal: The title was now exclusive, the rank specially adjusted; restraint and vigilance were applied with particular rigor in the Ming—and throughout the Qing, consort clans all strictly observed the law and did not interfere in government; this can only be called sound provision for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Once the title was reserved to them alone and the rank specially adjusted, restraint and vigilance were applied with particular rigor under the Ming; throughout the Qing as well, consort clans strictly observed the law and did not meddle in government—a policy that can only be called wise provision for posterity.

sentences.zh: 《明史》用班氏例，兼及宦官恩倖之得封者，尤清所未有，茲次第諸后族，爲外戚表，凡以外戚封及其家初有爵，以外戚進者，皆入焉。

translations.literal: The Ming History followed Ban's precedent and also included eunuchs favored with enfeoffment—something the Qing especially lacked. Here the various empress clans are arranged in order to form the Imperial In-Laws Table; all who received rank as in-laws, those whose families first held nobility through in-law status, and those advanced as in-laws—all are entered here.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming History followed Ban Gu's precedent and also included eunuchs who received enfeoffment through imperial favor—something the Qing especially did without. Here the various empress clans are arranged in order as the Imperial In-Laws Table; all enfeoffed as in-laws, those whose families first gained rank through in-law ties, and those advanced through in-law status are all entered here.

sentences.zh: 后族別以功封，仍列功臣世爵表。

translations.literal: Empress clans enfeoffed separately for merit are still listed in the Table of Hereditary Noble Ranks of Meritorious Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Empress clans enfeoffed separately for merit are still listed in the Table of Hereditary Noble Ranks of Meritorious Officials.
